origin.description: Extract every word, ignoring non-word boundary segments.
origin.usage: stri_extract_all_words(str, simplify = FALSE, omit_no_match = FALSE, locale = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: FALSE returns a list. TRUE pads a matrix with empty strings. NA pads with NA.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: TRUE returns an empty vector when there are no words.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

origin.details: Equivalent to stri_extract_all_boundaries with type word and skip_word_none TRUE. A missing string is a one-element NA vector. No words are one NA unless omit_no_match is TRUE.
origin.value: A list of character vectors, or a character matrix when simplify is not FALSE.
origin.example:
found <- stri_extract_all_words("one two")
cat(paste0('stri_extract_all_words("one two") returns ', paste(found[[1]], collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Extract every word, ignoring non-word boundary segments.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: False returns a list of character vectors. True pads with empty strings. NA pads with NA.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: True returns an empty vector when there are no words.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: None or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

translation.details: Calls stri_extract_all_boundaries with type word and skip_word_none true. A missing string is a one-element NA vector. No words are one NA unless omit_no_match is true. Thai segmentation warns because the bundle falls back to root.
translation.value: A list of character vectors, or a list of rows when simplify is not false.
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_extract_all_words
found = stri_extract_all_words("one two")
print('stri_extract_all_words("one two") returns ' + ", ".join(found[0]) + ".")
